text:
A young man came to an old teacher and complained about his life. “Everything is bitter,” he said. “My job is hard, my friends disappoint me, and I feel unhappy all the time.”

The teacher listened silently. Then he handed the young man a glass of water and a spoonful of salt. “Put the salt in the water and drink it,” he said.

The young man did so and immediately made a face. “It’s disgusting!”

The teacher smiled and led him to a small lake behind the house. “Now put the same amount of salt in the lake,” he said. The young man poured the salt into the water and stirred it with a stick.

“Now drink some of the lake water.”

The young man knelt down and drank from his hands. “It’s fresh,” he said, surprised. “I can’t taste the salt at all.”

“The salt was exactly the same,” said the teacher. “The pain in life is also the same for everybody. Troubles will always come. But how bitter they taste depends on the size of the container that holds them.”

The young man thought about this.

“When you feel unhappy, stop being a glass,” the teacher continued. “Become a lake. Widen your view. Think about your family, your health, and the beauty around you. Then the bitterness will become only a small part of a much bigger life.”

The young man went home with a lighter heart. From that day, whenever he felt miserable, he remembered the lake.

Moral: You cannot avoid pain, but you can make your mind big enough to hold it.

quiz.q: The salt water in the glass tasted disgusting.
The lake water tasted very salty.
